summary: ACK-window truncation causes incomplete terminal fragments on SSE resume behind edge proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running SSE streams resume after an intermediary disconnect but the final conclusion paragraphs are truncated or missing. This occurs when the client ACK window (keepalive/ack batching) is narrow and the request traverses the customer's edge proxy which does HTTP connection coalescing and early ACK aggregation.

Impact:
- Multiple users at DraftBoard see incomplete responses ~10-30% of the time on long streaming completions (500-2k tokens).
- Customer reports data loss in end-of-stream summaries for billing-relevant outputs.
- Customer is on Dedicated capacity in us-east; traffic is routed through a managed edge (customer-provided nginx reverse proxy).

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) serving redwood-alpha-7b and openllama-7b-q4 variants.
- Customer edge: nginx 1.22 with proxy_buffering on, proxy_http_version 1.1 and keepalive enabled.
- Client: browser-based app using EventSource for SSE and an in-house reconnect/ack-window logic that batches resume acknowledgement frames.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long-generation SSE request with stream=true and expect ~1.2k tokens.
2) Simulate transient network blip or force edge restart to drop connection after ~60s of streaming.
3) Client reconnects and issues resume with last-received-offset and a batched ACK of pending control frames.
4) Server resumes but final terminal fragments are missing or truncated in 1 out of 4 attempts.

Observed behavior:
- Server logs show resume accepted and chunks sent.
- Client-side EventSource shows a resume event and then stops after what appears to be a valid closing chunk, but the text in the last chunk is truncated mid-sentence.
- Edge proxy logs show multiple Connection: keep-alive / early ACK interactions and occasional 1xx proxy responses.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should rehydrate KV cache and stream the remaining tokens including finalizing punctuation/metadata.
- No truncation or missing closing paragraphs.

Attachments / logs included:
- Customer-supplied HTTP traces (sensitive redacted) and EventSource debug console: /attachments/SUP-992021/traces.zip
- Edge proxy access/error logs (excerpt) and request/response trace IDs

Notes on severity: customer flags this as high because the last paragraph often contains the billable summary and compliance statement.
investigation_notes: 03/12 10:22 - Triage: reproduced locally with a synthetic nginx proxy configured to aggregate client ACKs into a single short window. Observed packet reordering and mid-chunk truncation when ACK window merged framing boundaries.

03/12 14:05 - Collected server-side streaming traces (trace ids: srv-trace-7741, srv-trace-7749). KVCACHE priming on resume looks successful; trailing token batches appear to be enqueued but delivery stalls in the edge hop.

03/12 18:30 - Hypothesis: proxy early-ACK + HTTP pipelining/coalescing causes edge to collapse chunk boundaries; downstream EventSource parser treats last partial chunk as final and discards subsequent metadata control frame.

03/13 09:00 - Added packet capture at edge (pcap) during reproducible test. Observed a TCP FIN from the edge during in-flight chunk that causes client to receive truncated chunk and server to continue sending.
- Server TCP window remains open; client-side socket closed prematurely by nginx reverse proxy.

03/13 12:40 - SRE ran a canary bypass: traffic routed directly to Redwood edge (bypassing customer-provided nginx). Resume succeeds consistently with no truncation. This strongly implicates customer edge configuration.

03/14 08:15 - Reproduced with modified nginx config (proxy_buffering off, http2 disabled). Truncation rate dropped to <1%. Suggests proxy buffering and HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation are contributing factors.
comments: 2026-03-12 11:05 - Jordan Kim (Support): Thanks for the report, @DraftBoard. We can reproduce with a proxy in front of the connection. Can you share the nginx config and a redacted pcap?

2026-03-12 12:36 - Customer (Samantha Lee, DraftBoard): Uploaded edge config and a sample pcap to the ticket. Note: we have proxy_buffering enabled and use http2 fronting to the internet, terminating to http1 upstream.

2026-03-13 13:02 - Jordan Kim (Support): We've run controlled tests that reproduce the issue. Temporary mitigation: set proxy_buffering off for the streaming endpoint and ensure keepalive_timeout > 120s. Can you apply this in staging?
2026-03-13 15:10 - Customer (Samantha Lee): Applied change in staging, initial test shows reduced truncation. We'll schedule a prod deploy of the config change tonight and report back.

2026-03-14 09:20 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Confirmed canary bypass results. Filed runtime change to add more robust final-fragment heartbeat and a guard to emit explicit END markers on resume to make clients more tolerant of partial boundary collapse. PR: runtime#2142

2026-03-14 11:48 - Jordan Kim (Support): Proposed follow-ups: 1) Recommend customer deploy nginx config change (proxy_buffering off) 2) We will ship server-side explicit EOF-control-frame guard in next minor release 3) SRE to monitor resumed stream truncation rate for 72h post-release.
resolution: Mitigation steps provided to customer: instruct edge operators to disable proxy_buffering and avoid HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation for streaming endpoints; temporary keepalive increase. SRE implemented an explicit terminal-control-frame guard in runtime (see PR runtime#2142) to make resume resilient to collapsed boundaries. Root cause: interplay of edge proxy buffering, early ACK aggregation, and client-side batched ACK/reconnect behavior; full verification pending after prod config change and runtime release.
next_steps: Customer to deploy nginx config changes to prod and report truncation rate by 2026-03-16.
Engineering to land runtime patch (PR runtime#2142) and cut a minor release with explicit END control frames for resumed streams.
SRE to monitor /metrics/stream_resume_truncation and alert if >0.5% in us-east for 72h post-deploy.
Follow-up postmortem to be created if issue persists after both changes.
